verses.text: "But now listen, Jacob my servant, Israel whom I have chosen.
This is what the LORD says, the one who made you, who formed you in the womb, and who will help you: Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, Jeshurun whom I have chosen.
For I will pour water on the thirsty land and streams on the dry ground. I will pour my Spirit on your children and my blessing on your descendants.
They will spring up like grass in a meadow, like willow trees by flowing streams.
One will say, 'I belong to the LORD.' Another will call himself by the name of Jacob. Another will write on his hand, 'The LORD's,' and take the name of Israel."
This is what the LORD says, Israel's King and Redeemer, the LORD of Armies: "I am the first and I am the last. Apart from me there is no God.
Who is like me? Let him say so. Let him tell it and explain it to me, what has happened since I set up my ancient people. Let them tell what is coming and what will happen.
Do not tremble. Do not be afraid. Did I not tell you this long ago and announce it? You are my witnesses. Is there any God besides me? No, there is no other Rock. I know of none."
All who make idols are nothing, and the things they treasure are worthless. Those who speak for idols are blind and know nothing, so they will be put to shame.
Who would shape a god or cast an idol that cannot help anyone?
Look, all who worship it will be put to shame. The craftsmen are only human. Let them all gather together and take their stand. They will be terrified and put to shame together.

The blacksmith takes a tool and works with it over the coals. He shapes the idol with hammers, working it with his strong arm. He gets hungry and loses his strength. He drinks no water and grows tired.
The woodworker measures with a line and marks it out with a pencil. He shapes it with chisels and marks it with a compass. He shapes it like a man, a handsome human figure, to live in a shrine.
He cuts down cedars, or he picks a cypress or an oak. He lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest. He plants a pine tree, and the rain makes it grow.
Then people use it as fuel. They take some of it to warm themselves. They light a fire and bake bread. But they also make a god from it and worship it. They make an idol and bow down to it.
Half of the wood they burn in the fire. Over it they cook their meat. They roast it and eat until they are full. They also warm themselves and say, "Ah! I am warm. I can see the fire."
From the rest of the wood they make a god, their idol. They bow down to it and worship it. They pray to it and say, "Save me, for you are my god!"
They do not know or understand anything. Their eyes are closed so they cannot see, and their minds are closed so they cannot understand.

No one stops to think. No one has the knowledge or understanding to say, "Half of it I burned in the fire. I even baked bread on its coals. I roasted meat and ate it. Should I make something disgusting from the rest of it? Should I bow down to a block of wood?"
Such a person feeds on ashes. A deceived heart leads them astray. They cannot save themselves or say, "Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?"
"Remember these things, Jacob, for you, Israel, are my servant. I formed you. You are my servant. Israel, I will never forget you.
I have wiped away your sins like a thick cloud, your wrongdoing like the morning mist. Come back to me, for I have rescued you."

Sing for joy, you heavens, for the LORD has done this! Shout out loud, you depths of the earth! Burst into song, you mountains, you forests and all your trees! For the LORD has rescued Jacob, and he shows his glory in Israel.
This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer, who formed you in the womb: "I am the LORD, who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth by myself.
I make the signs of false prophets fail and make fools of fortune tellers. I turn back the wise and make their knowledge foolish.

I make the words of my servant come true and carry out the plans of my messengers. I say of Jerusalem, 'People will live there again,' and of the towns of Judah, 'They will be rebuilt. I will restore their ruins.'
I say to the deep waters, 'Dry up! I will dry up your rivers.'
I say of Cyrus, 'He is my shepherd, and he will do everything I want.' He will say of Jerusalem, 'Let it be rebuilt,' and of the temple, 'Let its foundations be laid.'"
